HC001.reason_for_consultation: Sore throat, painful swallowing and fever for 3 days.
symptoms: Fever up to 38.9 °C measured at home
physical_examination: Enlarged, erythematous palatine tonsils with white exudate bilaterally
No peritonsillar bulging and no uvular deviation

laboratory_results.test: Rapid group A streptococcal antigen test (throat swab)

other_investigations: Modified Centor score: 4 (tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes, fever, absence of cough; age 15–44 years adds 0 points)
HC001.clinical_assessment: Acute tonsillopharyngitis with a modified Centor score of 4 and a positive rapid streptococcal antigen test, confirming group A streptococcal infection. No signs of peritonsillar abscess or airway compromise. Suitable for outpatient oral antibiotic treatment.

prescribed_medications.name: Paracetamol
prescribed_medications.frequency: Every 8 hours as needed (maximum 3 g per day)

procedures: Throat swab for rapid streptococcal antigen test
treatment_recommendations: Complete the full 10-day antibiotic course even if symptoms improve
Maintain adequate oral fluid intake and rest
Avoid sharing cups and utensils
May return to work 24 hours after starting antibiotics if fever has resolved
HC001.clinical_progress: Initial consultation; treatment was started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
warning_signs: Inability to swallow saliva or drooling
Difficulty opening the mouth or one-sided throat swelling
Fever persisting more than 72 hours after starting antibiotics
HC001.follow_up_plan: Return for reassessment if there is no improvement within 72 hours or if any warning sign appears; no routine follow-up visit is required if symptoms resolve.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Inflammation of the tonsils and the back of the throat, usually caused by a viral or bacterial infection.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Inflamación de las amígdalas y de la parte posterior de la garganta, generalmente causada por una infección vírica o bacteriana.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Fluid, often whitish, that leaks from inflamed tissue and can be seen as patches on the tonsils.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Líquido, a menudo blanquecino, que sale de un tejido inflamado y puede verse como placas en las amígdalas.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A clinical scale that estimates the likelihood that a sore throat is caused by streptococcal bacteria.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Escala clínica que estima la probabilidad de que un dolor de garganta esté causado por bacterias estreptocócicas.

HC002.reason_for_consultation: Review of persistently elevated home blood pressure readings after 3 months of lifestyle measures.
medical_history: Elevated office blood pressure first recorded 3 months before this encounter
Former smoker; stopped smoking 10 years ago
family_history: Father with hypertension who had a stroke at age 70
symptoms: Denies headache, chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations and visual disturbances
physical_examination: Office blood pressure 154/96 mmHg (mean of two seated readings)
other_investigations: Home blood pressure monitoring over 7 days: mean 152/94 mmHg
12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, no signs of left ventricular hypertrophy
HC002.clinical_assessment: Hypertension confirmed by repeated office readings and home monitoring, without evidence of target organ damage (normal renal function, no albuminuria, no left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG). Blood pressure remains above target despite 3 months of lifestyle measures, so drug treatment is indicated.
treatment_recommendations: Limit salt intake to less than 5 g per day
Aerobic physical activity for at least 150 minutes per week
Gradual weight reduction
Limit alcohol intake
Continue home blood pressure log twice daily for 7 days before the next visit
HC002.clinical_progress: Home and office blood pressure readings did not reach target after 3 months of lifestyle measures.
HC002.response_to_treatment: Insufficient response to lifestyle modification; response to ramipril not yet assessed.
warning_signs: Severe headache with blood pressure of 180/110 mmHg or higher
Chest pain or shortness of breath
Sudden weakness, numbness, speech difficulty or vision loss
Swelling of the lips, tongue or face after starting ramipril
HC002.follow_up_plan: Review in 4 weeks with home blood pressure log and repeat serum creatinine and potassium to check tolerance of ramipril; titrate dose if blood pressure remains above target.

glossary_terms.definition_en: High blood pressure without an identifiable specific cause; it is the most common form of hypertension.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Presión arterial elevada sin una causa específica identificable; es la forma más frecuente de hipertensión.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A class of medicines that lower blood pressure by blocking the formation of a hormone that narrows blood vessels.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Grupo de medicamentos que reducen la presión arterial bloqueando la formación de una hormona que estrecha los vasos sanguíneos.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Harm caused by long-standing high blood pressure to organs such as the heart, kidneys, brain or eyes.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Daño causado por la presión arterial elevada mantenida en órganos como el corazón, los riñones, el cerebro o los ojos.

HC003.reason_for_consultation: Increased thirst, frequent urination and tiredness; review of blood test results.
physical_examination: Feet: intact skin without ulcers, normal 10 g monofilament sensation bilaterally
Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses present bilaterally
other_investigations: Diabetic retinal screening (retinography) requested; result pending
HC003.clinical_assessment: Osmotic symptoms with HbA1c of 7.8% and two fasting glucose values above 126 mg/dL confirm type 2 diabetes. Risk factors include obesity, previous gestational diabetes and a first-degree relative with diabetes. No evidence of nephropathy or peripheral neuropathy; retinal screening pending. Ketones negative.

prescribed_medications.name: Metformin
prescribed_medications.frequency: Once daily with the evening meal for 1 week, then twice daily with meals

treatment_recommendations: Referral to structured diabetes education programme
Reduce refined carbohydrates and sugary drinks
Aerobic physical activity for at least 150 minutes per week
Target weight loss of 5–10% of body weight
Daily foot inspection
HC003.clinical_progress: Initial diagnostic consultation; treatment started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
warning_signs: Vomiting, abdominal pain or rapid breathing
Persistent diarrhoea or abdominal discomfort after starting metformin
HC003.follow_up_plan: Nurse review in 4 weeks to check metformin tolerance; medical review in 3 months with repeat HbA1c and lipid profile; review retinal screening result when available.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A blood test that reflects the average blood glucose level over the previous 2–3 months.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Análisis de sangre que refleja el nivel medio de glucosa en sangre durante los 2–3 meses anteriores.

glossary_terms.definition_en: The production of abnormally large volumes of urine, leading to frequent urination.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Producción de volúmenes de orina anormalmente grandes, que provoca orinar con frecuencia.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A first-line oral medicine for type 2 diabetes that reduces glucose production by the liver.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Medicamento oral de primera línea para la diabetes tipo 2 que reduce la producción de glucosa por el hígado.

HC004.reason_for_consultation: Persistent nasal congestion and sneezing with episodes of wheezing and night-time cough.
medical_history: Episodic wheezing treated with as-needed salbutamol

current_medications.name: Salbutamol
current_medications.frequency: 2 inhalations as needed (currently used about 3 times per week)

HC004.symptom_onset: Gradual worsening over the past 3 months
HC004.symptom_frequency: Nasal symptoms daily; wheezing about 3 days per week; night-time awakenings twice per week
physical_examination: Pale, swollen nasal turbinates with clear discharge
Scattered expiratory wheeze on chest auscultation
No use of accessory respiratory muscles
other_investigations: Bronchodilator reversibility: FEV1 increase of 14% (320 mL) after salbutamol
Skin prick test: positive for house dust mite (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus); negative for grass pollen, cat and dog dander
HC004.primary_diagnosis: Persistent allergic rhinitis with allergic asthma (house dust mite sensitisation)
HC004.clinical_assessment: Reversible airflow obstruction and raised FeNO confirm asthma, which is partly controlled (daytime symptoms more than twice weekly and night-time awakenings). Persistent rhinitis with house dust mite sensitisation. Treatment should be stepped up to inhaled corticosteroid-containing therapy together with treatment of the upper airway.
treatment_provided: Intranasal corticosteroid and oral antihistamine started

prescribed_medications.name: Budesonide/formoterol
prescribed_medications.frequency: 1 inhalation twice daily plus 1 inhalation as needed for symptoms (maximum 12 inhalations per day)

prescribed_medications.name: Mometasone furoate nasal spray
prescribed_medications.dose: 50 micrograms per spray; 2 sprays in each nostril

treatment_recommendations: Stop using salbutamol; use budesonide/formoterol as reliever
House dust mite reduction measures: mite-impermeable bedding covers and washing bedding at 60 °C weekly
Follow the written asthma action plan
Avoid tobacco smoke exposure
HC004.clinical_progress: Initial specialist assessment; new treatment started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
HC004.response_to_treatment: Inadequate symptom control with as-needed salbutamol alone; response to new treatment not yet assessed.
warning_signs: Breathlessness that prevents speaking in full sentences
Reliever needed more than every 4 hours or providing little relief
HC004.follow_up_plan: Review in 6 weeks to assess asthma control, inhaler technique and rhinitis symptoms; consider allergen immunotherapy referral if rhinitis remains uncontrolled.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A breathing test that measures how much air a person can exhale and how quickly.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Prueba respiratoria que mide cuánto aire puede expulsar una persona y con qué rapidez.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A breath test that measures nitric oxide, a marker of allergic-type inflammation in the airways.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Prueba de aliento que mide el óxido nítrico, un marcador de inflamación de tipo alérgico en las vías respiratorias.

glossary_terms.definition_en: An anti-inflammatory medicine breathed into the lungs to reduce airway inflammation and prevent asthma attacks.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Medicamento antiinflamatorio que se inhala hacia los pulmones para reducir la inflamación de las vías respiratorias y prevenir las crisis de asma.

HC005.reason_for_consultation: Burning sensation behind the breastbone and acid regurgitation after meals and at night.

current_medications.name: Ibuprofen
current_medications.frequency: As needed, approximately twice per month

symptoms: Symptoms worse after large meals and when lying down
No black stools or vomiting of blood
other_investigations: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy not indicated at this stage because there are no alarm features
HC005.clinical_assessment: Typical reflux symptoms (heartburn and regurgitation) without alarm features in a patient under 60 years of age. Clinical diagnosis of GERD is suspected, pending response to an empirical trial of a proton pump inhibitor. Overweight and occasional NSAID use may contribute.
treatment_provided: Empirical proton pump inhibitor trial started
treatment_recommendations: Avoid eating within 3 hours of going to bed
Raise the head of the bed
Gradual weight reduction
Reduce alcohol, coffee and large fatty meals
Use paracetamol instead of ibuprofen for headaches
HC005.clinical_progress: Initial consultation; treatment started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
warning_signs: Vomiting blood or black, tarry stools
HC005.follow_up_plan: Review in 8 weeks to assess response to omeprazole; if symptoms persist despite treatment, consider referral for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy.

glossary_terms.definition_en: The backward flow of stomach contents into the oesophagus, which can cause heartburn.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Paso del contenido del estómago hacia el esófago, que puede causar ardor o acidez.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A class of medicines that reduce the production of stomach acid.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Grupo de medicamentos que reducen la producción de ácido en el estómago.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Warning symptoms, such as difficulty swallowing or bleeding, that suggest a more serious condition and need further tests.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Síntomas de alerta, como dificultad para tragar o sangrado, que sugieren una enfermedad más grave y requieren más pruebas.

HC006.reason_for_consultation: Lower back pain after lifting heavy boxes at work.
symptoms: Lower back pain without radiation below the knee
Pain worse with bending and lifting, relieved by rest
No numbness or tingling in the legs
No numbness in the saddle area
HC006.symptom_onset: Sudden, 5 days before the encounter, while lifting boxes at work
physical_examination: Tenderness and muscle spasm of the lumbar paravertebral muscles
Straight leg raise test negative bilaterally
Normal lower limb strength, reflexes and sensation
HC006.primary_diagnosis: Acute non-specific mechanical lower back pain
HC006.clinical_assessment: Acute mechanical lower back pain related to lifting, with a normal neurological examination and no red flags (no trauma, fever, weight loss, history of cancer, saddle anaesthesia or sphincter dysfunction). Imaging is not indicated. Favourable prognosis is expected with conservative management.
treatment_recommendations: Stay active and avoid bed rest
Apply local heat for pain relief
Gradual return to normal activities and work, avoiding heavy lifting for 2 weeks
Use safe lifting technique
HC006.clinical_progress: Initial consultation; treatment started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
warning_signs: Numbness in the groin or buttocks
Loss of bladder or bowel control
Weakness in one or both legs
Severe pain at night that does not improve with rest
HC006.follow_up_plan: Review in 2 weeks if pain has not improved; refer to physiotherapy if symptoms persist beyond 4–6 weeks.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A physical examination test in which the straightened leg is lifted to check for irritation of a spinal nerve root.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Prueba de exploración física en la que se eleva la pierna estirada para comprobar si existe irritación de una raíz nerviosa de la columna.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A rare emergency caused by compression of the nerve roots at the lower end of the spinal canal.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Urgencia poco frecuente causada por la compresión de las raíces nerviosas en la parte inferior del canal vertebral.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug; a medicine that reduces pain and inflammation.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Antiinflamatorio no esteroideo; medicamento que reduce el dolor y la inflamación.

HC007.reason_for_consultation: Burning on urination and frequent urge to urinate for 2 days.
HC007.primary_diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis)
HC007.clinical_assessment: Typical lower urinary tract symptoms with positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites in a non-pregnant woman without fever or flank pain, consistent with uncomplicated cystitis. No signs of pyelonephritis. Penicillin allergy considered in antibiotic choice. Urine culture sent to confirm the organism and susceptibility.
procedures: Midstream urine sample for dipstick and culture
treatment_recommendations: Drink adequate fluids
Complete the full antibiotic course
Paracetamol may be used for discomfort
HC007.clinical_progress: Initial consultation; treatment started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
warning_signs: Pain in the side or back (flank pain)
Symptoms not improving after 48 hours of antibiotics
HC007.follow_up_plan: Urine culture result to be reviewed in 48–72 hours and antibiotic adjusted if the organism is resistant; return earlier if warning signs appear.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Inflammation of the bladder, most often caused by a bacterial infection.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Inflamación de la vejiga, causada con mayor frecuencia por una infección bacteriana.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Substances produced by some bacteria in urine; their presence on a dipstick suggests a bacterial infection.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Sustancias producidas por algunas bacterias en la orina; su presencia en una tira reactiva sugiere una infección bacteriana.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A laboratory test that grows bacteria from a urine sample to identify them and test which antibiotics work.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Prueba de laboratorio que cultiva las bacterias de una muestra de orina para identificarlas y comprobar qué antibióticos son eficaces.

HC008.reason_for_consultation: Tiredness and breathlessness on exertion; review of blood test results.
medical_history: Heavy menstrual periods for approximately 1 year
symptoms: Shortness of breath on climbing stairs
HC008.symptom_onset: Gradual, approximately 3 months before the encounter
physical_examination: Soft systolic flow murmur at the left sternal border

laboratory_results.test: Anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (with normal total IgA)

secondary_diagnoses.diagnosis: Heavy menstrual bleeding as the probable cause of iron loss

HC008.clinical_assessment: Microcytic, hypochromic anaemia with very low ferritin and transferrin saturation confirms iron-deficiency anaemia. Heavy menstrual bleeding is the most likely cause; coeliac serology is negative and there are no gastrointestinal symptoms. The mild rise in platelets is consistent with iron deficiency. Haemodynamically stable; oral iron is appropriate.

prescribed_medications.name: Ferrous sulfate
prescribed_medications.frequency: Once daily on an empty stomach
prescribed_medications.duration: Until haemoglobin normalises, then for a further 3 months

treatment_recommendations: Take iron with water or orange juice, not with tea, coffee or milk
Iron-rich diet
Black stools are an expected effect of iron tablets
Referral to gynaecology for evaluation of heavy menstrual bleeding
HC008.clinical_progress: Initial diagnostic consultation; treatment started at this visit and progress has not yet been assessed.
warning_signs: Very heavy menstrual bleeding soaking a pad every hour
HC008.follow_up_plan: Repeat full blood count in 4 weeks to confirm haemoglobin is rising; review pelvic ultrasound result and gynaecology assessment; check ferritin after completing treatment.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A protein that stores iron; low blood levels indicate that the body's iron stores are depleted.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Proteína que almacena hierro; niveles bajos en sangre indican que las reservas de hierro del cuerpo están agotadas.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Anaemia in which red blood cells are smaller than normal, typically due to iron deficiency.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Anemia en la que los glóbulos rojos son más pequeños de lo normal, generalmente por falta de hierro.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A blood test value that measures the average size of red blood cells.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Valor de un análisis de sangre que mide el tamaño medio de los glóbulos rojos.

HC009.reason_for_consultation: Persistent hoarseness; review of laryngeal biopsy and staging results.
medical_history: Alcohol intake of 2–3 units per day
HC009.symptom_onset: Gradual, approximately 3 months before the encounter
physical_examination: Flexible videolaryngoscopy: irregular exophytic lesion on the middle third of the right vocal fold, not involving the anterior commissure
Normal mobility of both vocal folds

laboratory_results.test: Histopathology of right vocal fold biopsy (14/10/2026)

imaging_results: Contrast-enhanced CT of the neck: lesion confined to the right vocal fold, no laryngeal cartilage invasion, no cervical lymphadenopathy
CT of the chest: no pulmonary nodules or distant metastases
other_investigations: Clinical stage: cT1a N0 M0 (AJCC 8th edition)
HC009.primary_diagnosis: Dysphonia associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the glottis (right vocal fold), stage cT1a N0 M0
HC009.clinical_assessment: Progressive dysphonia caused by early-stage glottic squamous cell carcinoma confined to one vocal fold with normal mobility, confirmed by biopsy. Staging CT shows no nodal or distant spread. Smoking and alcohol are the main risk factors. Early glottic cancer has a good prognosis with single-modality treatment.
treatment_provided: Diagnosis and staging results discussed with the patient
Referral to the head and neck multidisciplinary tumour board
procedures: Direct microlaryngoscopy with biopsy of the right vocal fold (performed 14/10/2026)
treatment_recommendations: Multidisciplinary tumour board to decide between radiotherapy and transoral laser microsurgery
Referral to a smoking cessation programme
Reduce alcohol intake
Continue current antihypertensive medication
HC009.clinical_progress: Hoarseness unchanged since the biopsy; definitive cancer treatment has not yet started.
HC009.follow_up_plan: Case to be presented at the head and neck multidisciplinary tumour board on 06/11/2026; ENT appointment within 2 weeks to discuss the treatment decision.

glossary_terms.definition_en: Any change in voice quality, such as hoarseness, weakness or strain.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Cualquier alteración en la calidad de la voz, como ronquera, debilidad o esfuerzo al hablar.

glossary_terms.definition_en: The part of the larynx that contains the vocal folds and the space between them.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Parte de la laringe que contiene las cuerdas vocales y el espacio que hay entre ellas.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A type of cancer that arises from the flat cells lining surfaces such as the throat and larynx.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Tipo de cáncer que se origina en las células planas que recubren superficies como la garganta y la laringe.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A system that describes the size of a tumour (T), spread to lymph nodes (N) and distant spread (M).
glossary_terms.definition_es: Sistema que describe el tamaño del tumor (T), la afectación de los ganglios linfáticos (N) y la diseminación a distancia (M).

HC010.reason_for_consultation: Sudden severe chest pain at rest; emergency admission.
medical_history: Unprovoked deep vein thrombosis of the right leg in 2023, treated with rivaroxaban for 6 months and then stopped
family_history: Mother with recurrent deep vein thrombosis
symptoms: Crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm
HC010.symptom_onset: Sudden, at rest, 90 minutes before arrival at hospital
HC010.symptom_duration: 90 minutes before arrival; resolved after reperfusion
physical_examination: Diaphoretic and in pain on arrival
Clear lung fields; no signs of heart failure

laboratory_results.result: Not interpretable (sample taken during heparin therapy)

imaging_results: Emergency coronary angiography: thrombotic occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery; no significant atherosclerosis in the other coronary arteries
Transthoracic echocardiogram: inferior wall hypokinesia, left ventricular ejection fraction 50%
other_investigations: 12-lead ECG on arrival: ST-segment elevation of 2.5 mm in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in leads I and aVL
Continuous cardiac monitoring: no ventricular arrhythmias
HC010.primary_diagnosis: Inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to thrombotic occlusion of the right coronary artery

secondary_diagnoses.diagnosis: Hypercoagulable state: probable antiphospholipid syndrome (requires repeat antibody testing at 12 weeks for confirmation)

HC010.clinical_assessment: Inferior STEMI with markedly raised troponin and thrombotic right coronary occlusion in a young non-smoker without significant atherosclerosis. Previous unprovoked venous thrombosis, a family history of thrombosis and high-titre anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I antibodies suggest an underlying hypercoagulable state, probably antiphospholipid syndrome, which requires confirmation. Successful reperfusion with preserved left ventricular function.
treatment_provided: Aspirin 300 mg and ticagrelor 180 mg oral loading doses
Intravenous unfractionated heparin during the procedure

prescribed_medications.name: Ticagrelor
prescribed_medications.indication: Dual antiplatelet therapy after coronary stent

procedures: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention with thrombus aspiration and drug-eluting stent implantation in the proximal right coronary artery, with final TIMI grade 3 flow
treatment_recommendations: Haematology consultation regarding a long-term anticoagulation strategy
Cardiac rehabilitation programme
Do not stop antiplatelet medicines without consulting cardiology
Heart-healthy diet and gradual increase in physical activity
HC010.clinical_progress: Chest pain resolved immediately after reperfusion. During the first 72 hours the patient remained haemodynamically stable, without recurrent chest pain, arrhythmias or signs of heart failure.
HC010.response_to_treatment: Successful reperfusion with TIMI grade 3 flow and resolution of chest pain after primary PCI.
warning_signs: Recurrent chest pain lasting more than 5 minutes
Bleeding that does not stop or black stools
HC010.follow_up_plan: Cardiology review 4 weeks after discharge; haematology review with repeat antiphospholipid antibody and lupus anticoagulant testing at least 12 weeks after the first test; enrolment in cardiac rehabilitation.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A heart attack in which a coronary artery is completely blocked, shown by ST-segment elevation on the ECG.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Infarto de miocardio en el que una arteria coronaria está completamente obstruida, lo que se refleja en una elevación del segmento ST en el electrocardiograma.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A procedure that opens a blocked coronary artery using a catheter, a balloon and usually a stent.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Procedimiento que abre una arteria coronaria obstruida mediante un catéter, un balón y, generalmente, un stent.

glossary_terms.definition_en: An autoimmune condition in which antibodies increase the tendency of blood to form clots in veins or arteries.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Enfermedad autoinmune en la que ciertos anticuerpos aumentan la tendencia de la sangre a formar coágulos en venas o arterias.

glossary_terms.definition_en: A heart muscle protein released into the blood when the heart muscle is damaged.
glossary_terms.definition_es: Proteína del músculo cardíaco que se libera a la sangre cuando el músculo del corazón sufre daño.
